subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class group authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the issue changes Slack access-control semantics and explicitly raises Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests, leaving defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

options.title: Reject Private-Channel Boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open group authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer To Broader Access Design
options.body: Track this under a broader channel authorization redesign if maintainers want cross-channel policy semantics instead of a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests, leaving defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact security/product gap and has the strongest visible adjacent history on group-policy and Slack security surfaces.
